encounters.cc: Increasing fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine

lines: Increasing fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine
The patient is a 33-year-old male with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency and IgA nephropathy who was evaluated two months prior for dark urine.
He presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of increasing fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine.
He reports a recent upper respiratory tract infection that resolved without treatment one week ago.
He denies any history of similar symptoms in the past.
- HIV/AIDS (CDC Stage 3, diagnosed age 32, currently non-adherent to ART)
- Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir alafenamide Non-adherent (discontinued 1 year ago due to insurance loss)
His family history is notable for a cousin with a "blood disorder" that the patient knows little about.
On physical examination, he is afebrile, with a heart rate of 102 bpm and blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg.
His sclerae are icteric, and his abdomen is soft with no hepatosplenomegaly.
- Peripheral blood smear: Presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies

lines: Increasing fatigue, shortness of breath, and dark urine after taking aspirin-containing medication

encounters.cc: Progressively worsening vision in right eye described as 'curtain coming down' with flashes and floaters

lines: Progressively worsening vision in right eye described as 'curtain coming down' with flashes and floaters
This 35-year-old male with HIV/AIDS (CDC Stage 3), recurrent G6PD hemolysis, and IgA nephropathy presents with progressively worsening vision.
He describes the vision changes as a "curtain coming down" over his field of vision, accompanied by flashes of light and an increase in floaters.
He has not been on antiretroviral therapy for the past year due to loss of insurance.
- Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin and soft tissue infection (diagnosed 2021-09-15)

encounters.cc: Sharp central chest pain worsening with inspiration and lying flat after upper respiratory infection

lines: Sharp central chest pain worsening with inspiration and lying flat after upper respiratory infection
Patient is a 35-year-old male with G6PD deficiency, IgA nephropathy, and HIV/AIDS (Stage 3) non-adherent to ART with recent CMV esophagitis.
He presents to emergency department with 2-day history of sharp, central chest pain worsening with deep inspiration and when lying flat.
He reports low-grade fever and recent upper respiratory tract infection.
- Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin and soft tissue infection (diagnosed 2021-09-15)
- HIV/AIDS (CDC Stage 3, diagnosed age 32, currently non-adherent to ART)
- Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir alafenamide Non-adherent (discontinued 1 year ago due to insurance loss)
On examination, his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 100 bpm, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and temperature is 37.8°C (100°F).
Cardiac examination reveals a pericardial friction rub.
An echocardiogram shows no evidence of tamponade or left ventricular dysfunction.
An ECG shows diffuse ST-segment elevations and PR depressions.

encounters.cc: Progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and lower extremity edema

lines: Progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and lower extremity edema

The 36-year-old male with G6PD deficiency, IgA nephropathy, HIV/AIDS with ART non-adherence, and prior pericarditis presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and lower extremity edema.
He reports a recent upper respiratory tract infection that resolved 1 week ago.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin and soft tissue infection (diagnosed 2021-09-15)
- HIV/AIDS (CDC Stage 3, diagnosed age 32, currently non-adherent to ART)
- Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir alafenamide Non-adherent (discontinued 1 year ago due to insurance loss)
His blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm, respiratory rate is 22 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air
Cardiac auscultation reveals a third heart sound (S3) gallop, and there are bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation.
Chest X-ray demonstrates cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion.
An echocardiogram shows biventricular enlargement with an ejection fraction of 30% and diffuse hypokinesis without valvular abnormalities.
